gemini.performance_metric: CorePoint sold in going-private transaction for $15.99/share
gemini.rationale: The slice documents the post-deal trajectory of the two successor entities (Wyndham and CorePoint). There is no documented evidence of product/process disruption (p4_pathway) or process/organization fracture (p5_pathway). The management agreements were terminated for a fee upon CorePoint's sale, but the franchise agreements remained in place, and there is no mention of operational integration failures or cultural clashes.

grok.performance_metric: CorePoint going-private ~3.75 yrs; La Quinta brand retained/grew to 922 props
grok.rationale: The slice documents no product/process interface disruption: under Wyndham the La Quinta brand scaled modestly to 922 properties/90,098 rooms by FY2021 from ~890/~87,500 at spin-off, and franchise agreements with the CorePoint hotels were retained and assumed by the new owner rather than terminated. No process/organization fracture is documented either: LQ Management continued managing all CorePoint hotels under the 2018 agreements through FY2020 (earning a 5% fee), and those management agreements were terminated only concurrently with CorePoint’s March 2022 going-private sale for an ~$84–85 million termination fee, a commercial exit rather than an operational/cultural break.

openai.performance_metric: CorePoint sold for $15.99 per share after approximately 3.75 years
openai.rationale: No product/process disruption is documented: by FY2021, the La Quinta brand had grown to 922 properties, and the franchise agreements remained in place when CorePoint was sold. No process/organization fracture is documented: the Wyndham subsidiary continued managing all CorePoint hotels through FY2020, and the management agreements were terminated only in connection with CorePoint’s March 2022 sale, for an approximately $84–85 million fee.
